title: Properties of ILP stability
html:
Remark. Properties of ILP stability

Independence of neighborhood. Stability is a fixed-q property. It does not require the ILP to be feasible on a neighborhood of q. An atom may be stable at q_0 and unstable at q_0 + \epsilon without contradiction. Stability tracks ILP-feasibility pointwise.

Connection to LP-feasibility. The continuous LP relaxation (x \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^N, \mathrm{G}(q) x \geq 0) is always feasible, since the trivial identity normal form T_e = e_{(k)} has y_{(k)} = 0. The ILP version is strictly stronger. The proton derivation in mass-endomorphism-tower shows that the 9-crossing element \mathcal{B}_3 \times \Delta_3(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) violates Frobenius positivity (it is LP-infeasible at integer values). An ILP search adjoining \{\sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_-\} finds the unique integer solution \sigma_0 \to \sigma_0 (2 gluon crossings) that restores stability.

Confined operators only. We solve the ILP within the confinement filtration (confinement level) at q. We only consider primitives e_\lambda in J^{\ell(K, q)}(q), since operators above the atom's confinement level are unavailable without further phase transitions.
